citation: Chen YY, Chen F, Chang SS, Wong J, Yip PSF. Assessing the Efficacy of Restricting Access to Barbecue Charcoal for Suicide Prevention in Taiwan: A Community-Based Intervention Trial. PLoS ONE. 2015;10(8):e0133809. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0133809.
title: Assessing the Efficacy of Restricting Access to Barbecue Charcoal for Suicide Prevention in Taiwan: A Community-Based Intervention Trial
abstract: Community-based quasi-experimental evaluation of a charcoal-restriction programme in New Taipei City compared with two control cities.
population: residents of New Taipei City, Taipei City, and Kaohsiung City, Taiwan
intervention_or_exposure: restricted retail access to barbecue charcoal
comparator: two comparison cities without the charcoal-restriction programme

effect_estimates.measure: simulation estimate of lives saved during 20 months

uncertainty: Quasi-experimental city-level design rather than random allocation.
Intervention effect estimates depend on secular-trend adjustment and comparison-city assumptions.
methods: generalized linear regression with secular trends

evidence_claims.statement: After adjustment for secular trends, the New Taipei charcoal-restriction programme was associated with an estimated 30% reduction in charcoal-burning suicide compared with the pre-intervention period.
evidence_claims.population: residents of New Taipei City, Taipei City, and Kaohsiung City, Taiwan
evidence_claims.intervention_or_exposure: restricted retail access to barbecue charcoal

provenance.locator: PubMed PMID 26305374, Abstract: Methods and Findings

evidence_claims.statement: The study reported no compensatory increase in non-charcoal-burning suicide in New Taipei City during the intervention period.
evidence_claims.population: residents of New Taipei City, Taipei City, and Kaohsiung City, Taiwan
evidence_claims.intervention_or_exposure: restricted retail access to barbecue charcoal

provenance.locator: PubMed PMID 26305374, Abstract: Methods and Findings

limitations: Short post-intervention evaluation window relative to later follow-up work.
applicability: Population-level means-restriction policy in settings where charcoal burning is a common suicide method.
safety_boundaries: Do not translate population suicide-rate changes into individual risk estimates.
Do not use this record to provide instructions about self-harm methods.
